reuse.why: Most actions share getBudgetableCategories and reuse existing budget, sheet, batching, and undo helpers, but copyPreviousMonth independently implements category eligibility.

duplication.why: The change consolidates most category selection and the six/twelve-month wrappers, but duplicates eligibility in copyPreviousMonth and the action-running test helper.

placement.why: Budget selection and calculations remain in actions.ts, with method registration and undo integration in app.ts following existing layering.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested month-wide actions, their arguments, supporting tests, or release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selection helper is useful, but maintaining a parallel eligibility implementation for copyPreviousMonth makes future rule changes unnecessarily fragile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getBudgetableCategories and independently checks income, visibility, saved templates, and fixed groups.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts expresses category eligibility through SQL and a filter in getBudgetableCategories, then reshapes the same decision into early-return guards over budget rows in copyPreviousMonth.

abstraction_drift.where: getBudgetableCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories option and its conditional SQL visibility clause, while copyPreviousMonth separately evolves the same eligibility rules instead of sharing their definition.
